newsitem.title: JORDAN: Israeli witnesses recount Jordan border shooting.
newsitem.headline: Israeli witnesses recount Jordan border shooting.

text.p: An Israeli schoolgirl injured when a Jordanian soldier went on a shooting spree last March, killing seven of her colleagues, on Monday described her ordeal to a military court.
"We went off the bus and stood close to the guide who began to explain...and talked for nearly a minute until we heard the shots," Maya Sameul, 14, told the court in a soft voice.

The girl and other witnesses were brought under heavy security to testify in the trial of Private Ahmed Daqamsa, who shot the Israeli girls in the Jordanian border territory of Baqoura leased to Israel under a 1994 peace treaty.
Maya, speaking only a few metres away from where a composed Daqamsa was sitting in a chair behind the black bars of his cage, said a bullet which he fired hit her in the stomach.
Maya, who was rushed to a local hospital to stop internal bleeding, said she later "woke up in hospital (in Israel) where I stayed for two months."
Another group of schoolgirls who went on the trip to the lush farmland area last March, will testify at the next hearing on Sunday.

Daqamsa has not denied shooting the girls, six of them aged 13 and one just 11 years old, but says he acted impulsively after being provoked during Moslem prayers. He faces a death sentence if found guilty on four charges including premeditated murder and military disobedience.

Zeiv Kramer, 45, the trip guide who lives in the nearby Kibbutz Gesher, recalled how he at first thought Daqamsa, who was preparing his M16 rifle to shoot, was only removing an ammunition clip until it dawned on him that he "was shooting at us.

"At first when I saw him handling his ammunition clip and I thought he wanted to remove it. I wanted to continue talking to the girls but then after four, five seconds I heard a volley of automatic fire," said Kramer.

The court also heard the testimony of Jaffa Shakroun, 40, a Hebrew language school teacher who was shot in her left arm and rushed unconscious with Maya to the same local hospital before being airlifted by an Israeli plane.

"When we rushed to hide under the slope, a girl screamed saying she was very pained and as she got closer I saw her head down, at the same time my left shoulder was hit by a bullet and I lost consciousness," she said.
Asked by the defence lawyer why the schoolgroup was visiting the area, Shakroun said: "The girls wanted to see the site which is in their syllabus, taking advantage of the peace."

Military judge Brigadier Mamoun al-Khasawneh turned down a request by defence lawyer Hussein Majjali to bar Israeli witnesses on grounds Jews would not say the truth because they were the "eternal enemies" of Arabs.

The defence counsel also protested the refusal of most of the Israeli witnesses to give an oath by the Jewish holy book Torah before testifying which they said was in line with religious beliefs. But the judge again brushed aside his objection.
